children: Technology companies continue to operate in an environment influenced by increasing digitalization, growing adoption of connected technologies and evolving customer requirements across industrial and commercial markets. Against this backdrop,
Acorn Energy, Inc.
ACFN and
Powerfleet, Inc.

AIOT are two technology companies serving different end markets with distinct operating models. ACFN provides remote monitoring and control solutions for critical infrastructure assets, with a focus on power generation equipment and pipeline monitoring applications through its OmniMetrix subsidiary. In contrast, AIOT provides Artificial Intelligence-of-Things solutions for managing high-value enterprise and mid-market assets through its Unity platform and related offerings.

While both companies provide technology-driven asset monitoring and management solutions, their product offerings and end-market exposure differ. Acorn focuses primarily on power generation and pipeline monitoring, while Powerfleet serves a broader range of enterprise and mobile assets. These differences shape each company's investment appeal. This raises an important question: which stock is better positioned for investors today? Let's take a closer look.
Stock Performance & Valuation: ACFN vs. AIOT
ACFN (up 15.3%) has outperformed AIOT (down 23.1%) over the past three months. In the past year, Acorn stock has lost 29.9% compared with Powerfleet’s plunge of 35.4%.

Meanwhile, ACFN is trading at a trailing 12-month enterprise value-to-sales (EV/S) ratio of 4.6X, above its median of 2.8X over the past five years. AIOT’s trailing 12-month EV/S multiple sits at 1.3X, below its last five-year median of 1.4X. ACFN and AIOT both appear to be cheap when compared with the Zacks Computer and Technology sector’s average of 8.3X.
Factors Driving Acorn Stock

Acorn’s recurring monitoring business provides a strong foundation for growth and profitability. Monitoring revenues are supported by an expanding installed base and ongoing customer renewals, providing greater revenue visibility than hardware sales. The higher-margin nature of monitoring revenues also supports a favorable revenue mix and operating leverage as the business scales, helping ACFN maintain profitability despite variability in hardware deployments.

OMNI360 meaningfully broadens Acorn’s opportunity beyond its traditional generator and pipeline-monitoring businesses. The platform integrates power, environmental and security monitoring, remote controls and AI-supported capabilities into a unified solution for cell tower campuses and other critical infrastructure. By extending ACFN’s capabilities from individual asset monitoring to broader site-level infrastructure management, OMNI360 expands the company’s addressable market and creates an additional avenue for long-term growth.

The Champion Power Equipment partnership strengthens Acorn’s reach in the residential standby-generator market. OmniMetrix is now the standard monitoring option on Champion’s aXis and fleX generator lines, providing ACFN with an additional channel to reach customers. Management expects the partnership to contribute to results while strengthening the company’s presence in a growing residential generator market.
Factors Aiding Powerfleet Stock

Powerfleet’s growing services business is strengthening the quality and predictability of its revenue base. Services remain the company’s primary growth engine and are becoming a larger part of the overall business. The shift toward higher-margin recurring services is also supporting gross-margin expansion and should provide greater operating leverage as AIOT scales its SaaS-oriented business model.

Powerfleet is deepening relationships with existing enterprise customers through cross-selling and broader adoption of its Unity solutions. Recent expansions span on-site offerings, AI video and other solutions across diverse industries. Leveraging established customer relationships to broaden product adoption can increase wallet share while reinforcing Unity’s position as an integrated platform for customers seeking greater visibility, safety and operational efficiency.

The South African National Treasury contract represents a significant expansion opportunity for Powerfleet. Deployment demand has accelerated well beyond initial expectations, prompting the company to redirect resources from less strategic business toward the larger opportunity. Successful execution will likely expand AIOT’s deployed asset base and provide a stronger foundation for growth as the contract ramps.
Choose ACFN Over AIOT Now

Both Acorn and Powerfleet are positioned to benefit from growing adoption of connected asset-monitoring technologies, but ACFN currently presents a more focused investment proposition. Its high-margin recurring monitoring business provides a solid foundation, while OMNI360 expands the company into broader critical-infrastructure applications. The Champion partnership further extends its market reach, giving Acorn multiple avenues to build on its core monitoring capabilities.

AIOT also has meaningful growth opportunities, supported by recurring services, cross-selling and broader adoption of its Unity solutions. However, its near-term investment case involves greater execution complexity. The accelerated South African National Treasury rollout has required Powerfleet to redirect resources from less strategic business, contributing to a revision in its near-term outlook even as management maintains its longer-term growth expectations.

From a valuation perspective, AIOT appears relatively more inexpensive against its historical levels, whereas ACFN trades at a higher valuation. This suggests investors considering Acorn are paying more for its growth prospects, leaving less room for execution disappointments. However, ACFN's stronger recent stock performance, focused recurring-revenue model and expanding growth avenues help offset this valuation concern.

Considering these factors, Acorn appears to be the smarter buy right now. Its recurring monitoring strength, infrastructure expansion opportunities and stronger recent market performance provide a more compelling overall investment case, although Powerfleet's lower valuation remains attractive for investors willing to accept greater near-term execution risk.
